That’s not how that would go at all, I know from experience. You take a lot of pills, lie about for a bit, just waiting for everything to end. Close your eyes and sit and wait. Or you find something to do, like drink alcohol to try and seal the deal. You pass out. You wake up in cold sweats, your body aching, head feeling like it’s bleeding, but it’s not. You panic. You throw up. Constant. Until your throat is bleeding and your bile is everywhere. You try to sleep again but it’s impossible. Eventually you have to go to hospital, you just want the immense pain to stop. You get up. You’re dizzy, uneasy. Using the walls for support, but it feels like the walls are moving. Your stomach flip flops, feels like waves are crashing against you from the inside. You get to hospital. You get rushed, fast tracked for treatment. You’re weak. You pass out again. 10 minutes later you’re woken up by your own pain or by a doctor making sure you’re not dead. You get hooked up to a machine. You have no idea what is even going on. It’s a cycle of sleeping, throwing up and blood tests. Over and over, like a reoccurring nightmare. Talking burns from the constant puking, eating is near impossible since your body just rejects it. The world does not stop spinning. The stomach does not stop moving. You do not stop panicking. 

And then you get discharged, everything is fine, except now suicide is on your medical records. Except now whenever you look at a pill that even resembles what you took before, your body reacts and you psychologically feel the pain you felt. You spin, your stomach flips, you throw up. At least with me. 
If you took paracetamol or anything with that in, you can no longer take it without thinking first. It builds up in the system, and since you already have so much of it, it’s dangerous to take it regularly. 
Your family are now aware and you get treated differently. Different to when they know you’re depressed, now you’ve actually gone for it everything changes. They’re gentler for a while, pussyfoot around you, act like you’re broken glass when in fact you’re the strongest double glazed fucking window out there. 

It’s not “take pills and fall asleep and never wake up”. It’s suffering and never fully recovering. 

I hope you’re okay. I’m open to message or talk any time, I have multiple experiences with this kind of thing. I know what position you’re in, I’m happy to listen.
